_policy: Every continue-on-error in a workflow carries a disposition: ratchet (a number that may not rise), expires (a date by which someone must decide again), or conditional (soft here, hard somewhere that matters). Enforced by scripts/check-gate-policy.py. Reasoning: docs/testing/gaps.md G3/G4.

ci.yml::frontend-lint-type-test::Audit a.why: Build-time tools (Vite and friends) run on the build machine, not in what ships, and are noisy: 22 advisories on the 25 Nov 2026 review. The shipped-dependency audit was split out and made blocking that day. At the next review, decide whether any of these has sat unaddressed long enough to matter.

ci.yml::gates.why: Job-level `continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.soft == true }}`, and mypy is the only cell that sets it. Same disposition it had as a step before the 3 Sep split into a fail-fast:false matrix — 238 errors (3 Sep 2026) was a project, not a commit, so the count is held instead, by the hard ratchet cell, whose ceiling is now 0. If a second cell is ever marked soft, this single key stops describing it and the entry must be split.

ci.yml::supply-chain::Audit dependencies.why: Upstream CVEs are not ours to fix on demand, so a failure here is news rather than a defect. Reviewed 25 Nov 2026: pip-audit clean on CI that day, so nothing had sat unaddressed; re-dated to the next quarterly review. Promote it if it stays clean through two reviews.

ci.yml::supply-chain::Generate Python SB.why: Artifact generation, not a correctness check: a failure means no SBOM was published, which matters for the verifiable-security-claim track and nothing else. Revisit when that track needs the SBOM to be reliable.
